title: What If the World's Wheat Harvest Failed for a Whole Year?

scenes.text: What if the world's wheat harvest failed for a year? One calorie in five would be gone.
Wheat supplies about 20 percent of all calories people eat, and 20 percent of protein.
About 2.5 billion people in 89 countries depend on it.
The world grew roughly 811 million tons of it in 2022, on 219 million hectares.
About two thirds goes straight to human food, around 69 kilograms per person every year.
No other single crop fills that gap, so a failed year would hit the plates of billions at once.
